paper_title: Predicting reaction performance in C-N cross-coupling using machine learning

key_components.catalyst: Palladium complexes formed in situ from a Pd source and phosphine ligands
key_components.ligand: Four different Buchwald biaryl phosphine ligands

mechanistic_insights: The inhibitory effect of isoxazole additives is strongly correlated with their electrophilicity, with key predictive features being the additive's C-3 NMR shift, LUMO energy, and electrostatic charges.

A deleterious side reaction was identified where highly electrophilic isoxazoles undergo competitive N-O bond oxidative addition to the Pd(0) catalyst, effectively poisoning it and reducing the yield of the desired amination.

Random forest machine learning models significantly outperform traditional linear regression for predicting reaction yields, indicating that the relationships between component features and outcomes are highly non-linear.
The machine learning model demonstrated strong 'out-of-sample' predictive power, successfully forecasting the performance of new isoxazole additives not included in the original training set.

The random forest model maintained high predictive accuracy even with sparse training data (e.g., 5% of the full dataset), suggesting ML can be a practical tool for reaction optimization without exhaustive high-throughput screening.

quantitative_outcomes.notes: The primary quantitative outcome was the performance of the predictive model. The random forest algorithm achieved a high coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.92 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 7.8% yield on the test set. This significantly outperformed linear regression (R² = 0.64, RMSE = 16.3%). The model also showed strong performance in predicting the effect of new, unseen additives (average R² = 0.83).
